newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia moves step closer to protective tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Estonia moves step closer to protective tariffs.

text.p: Estonia's government on Tuesday approved in principle a plan for customs duty legislation, bringing it a step closer to the imposition of its first protective tariffs.
The plan calls for the adoption this year of a law on customs tariffs.
The setting of import tariffs would be a radical move for Estonia, which has boasted of its very open economy since quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991.
Since then it has had virtually no import tariffs although rural politicians have demanded tariffs for a long time, saying they need the protection from foreign imports.
"If passed, a customs duty law would establish the order in which tariffs may be established," Agriculture Minister Andres Varik told a news conference.
Varik said there was no decision yet on whether the law will define the levels of tariffs as well.
An import duty law has so far only been discussed by parliament's economic commission and the government will discuss the laws needed at its next session on April 22, Varik added.
A government commission in March proposed the establishment of 30 to 35 percent tariffs on imported pork and said it was the only agricultural sector where tariffs may be effective.
